problem:
Consider the line $y=-1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=-8.$
worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=-1$ passes through the points $P(0,-1)$ and $Q(1,-1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${P}^{′}(0,2)$ and ${Q}^{′}(4,3).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${P}^{′}$ and ${Q}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-2 & =\frac{3-2}{4-0}(x-0) \\ y-2 & =\frac{1}{4}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4y-8 & =x \\ x-4y & =-8\end{aligned}
$$
